chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who is killed while he owes a debt and has no property. Do his heirs have the right to forgo his blood in favor of his killer while he still has a debt?

He said: “Indeed, the holders of the debt are the litigants against the killer. So if his heirs forgo his blood in favor of his killer, they must guarantee the debt to the creditors; otherwise, they may not.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَائِهِ: His legal heirs or those entitled to act regarding his blood claim.
key_terms.الْخُصَمَاءُ: The litigants or claimants in the legal dispute.
key_terms.دَمَهُ: His blood, meaning the claim arising from his killing.
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: A financial debt owed by the deceased.
key_terms.ضَمِنُوا: They become responsible to cover or guarantee payment.
key_terms.لِلْغُرَمَاءِ: For the creditors, meaning those to whom the debt is owed.

ai.seo_question: Can the heirs of a murdered debtor forgive the killer if the deceased left unpaid debt and no property?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a murdered person who leaves behind debt but no wealth. It establishes that the rights of creditors are attached to the case, so the heirs cannot waive retaliation or blood-compensation rights in a way that nullifies the creditors’ claims unless they themselves assume liability for the debt.
